comparisons.peer_topic: BofAS Net Capital Requirements and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: BofAS, which provides institutional services, is required to maintain tentative net capital above $5.0 billion and net capital exceeding the greater of $1.0 billion or a percentage of its reserve requirement; at December 31, 2024, it held tentative net capital of $23.6 billion and regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, exceeding its minimum requirement of $4.5 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS&Co) and Bank of America (BofAS) are U.S. broker-dealers that have elected to calculate their SEC minimum capital requirements using the 'Alternative Net Capital Requirement' framework. Both entities are subject to specific minimums for tentative net capital (in excess of $5.0 billion) and net capital (in excess of $1.0 billion). However, their actual capital positions differed materially as of December 2024: GS&Co reported regulatory net capital of $21.31 billion (exceeding minimums by $15.87 billion), while BofAS reported regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion (exceeding its minimum requirement of $4.5 billion). Additionally, BofAS explicitly discloses a $6.0 billion notification threshold for tentative net capital, similar to GS&Co's notification requirements.

sentences.text: GS&Co., our primary U.S. regulated broker-dealer subsidiary, is also a registered futures commission merchant and a registered swap dealer with the CFTC, and a registered security-based swap dealer with the SEC, and therefore is subject to regulatory capital requirements imposed by the SEC, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc., the CFTC, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and the National Futures Association.

GS&Co. had regulatory net capital, as defined by Rule 15c3-1 of the SEC, of $21.31 billion as of December 2024 and $20.25 billion as of December 2023, which exceeded the greater of the minimum amounts required under Rule 15c3-1 of the SEC and Rules 1.17 and Part 23 Subpart E of the CFTC by $15.87 billion as of December 2024 and $15.07 billion as of December 2023.

BofAS provides institutional services, and in accordance with the alternative net capital requirements, is required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion and net capital in excess of the greater of $1.0 billion or a certain percentage of its reserve requirement in addition to a certain percentage of securities-based swap risk margin.
BofAS also had regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, which exceeded the minimum requirement of $4.5 billion.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory capital requirements for J.P. Morgan Securities
comparisons.peer_summary: J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to net capital requirements under the SEC's Net Capital Rule (Rule 15c3-1), has elected to compute minimum net capital using Alternative Net Capital Requirements, and as a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, must maintain tentative net capital above $5.0 billion and notify regulators if it falls below $6.0 billion.
comparisons.comparison: J.P. Morgan Securities, like Goldman Sachs' GS&Co, is a primary U.S. broker-dealer subsidiary subject to SEC Rule 15c3-1 and has elected to compute minimum net capital using 'Alternative Net Capital Requirements.' Both entities are registered as swap dealers and security-based swap dealers, which subjects them to alternative minimum net capital requirements, including holding tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion and notifying regulators if it falls below $6.0 billion. In terms of actual compliance, both firms maintained tentative net capital in excess of these minimum and notification requirements as of December 31, 2024.

sentences.text: GS&Co., our primary U.S. regulated broker-dealer subsidiary, is also a registered futures commission merchant and a registered swap dealer with the CFTC, and a registered security-based swap dealer with the SEC, and therefore is subject to regulatory capital requirements imposed by the SEC, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc., the CFTC, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and the National Futures Association.
As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GS&Co. had tentative net capital and net capital in excess of both the minimum and the notification requirements.
J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to the regulatory capital requirements of Rule 15c3-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Net Capital Rule").
J.P. Morgan Securities has elected to compute its minimum net capital requirements in accordance with the "Alternative Net Capital Requirements" of the Net Capital Rule.
